key_insight: ShipNet uses geometric deep learning on hull point clouds to rapidly surrogate ship hydrodynamics, predicting both local pressure and far-field wave patterns from geometry and speed.
engineering_relevance: This enables near real-time design-space exploration for ship hull optimization, replacing expensive potential-flow CFD with fast, high-accuracy predictions.
method: Regularized dynamic graph convolution on hull point clouds
Multi-head decoder for pressure coefficient and free-surface elevation
Composite loss combining point-wise regression and image-structure terms
evidence_signal: Trained on 420 potential-flow simulations from two parent yacht hulls with 70 variants each at three speeds, and evaluated on a geometry-held-out test set with R^2=0.98 for pressure and R^2=0.91 for waves.
watch_item: Performance is limited to the tested hull families, speed range, and inviscid training data, so generalization to unseen geometries or viscous flows remains uncertain.
paper_title: ShipNet: A Geometric Deep Learning Surrogate for Real-Time Ship Hydrodynamics
